summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding Indian bank holidays and their impact on financial transactions, with most claims verified against official sources.

claims.claim: For the week of June 14 to June 21, 2026, there are designated bank holidays that will lead to branch closures.
claims.note: June 14, 2026, is a Sunday (weekly holiday). June 15, 2026, has regional holidays (YMA Day/Raja Sankranti). June 21, 2026, is a Sunday (weekly holiday).

claims.claim: Bank holidays in India are primarily categorised under three types, as specified by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
claims.note: While the RBI website lists holidays, it doesn't explicitly categorize them into these three types with these specific names. Holidays are generally declared under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

claims.claim: Holidays under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. On these days, all public and private sector banks remain closed for public transactions.
claims.note: Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, states that if the maturity date of a promissory note or bill of exchange falls on a public holiday, it is deemed to be due on the preceding business day. Public holidays include Sundays and days declared by the government.

claims.claim: RTGS transactions, typically used for large-value transfers (₹2 lakhs and above), might be affected on these specific days. However, the RBI has been moving towards 24x7 availability for many digital payment systems.
claims.note: RTGS has been available 24x7x365 with effect from December 14, 2020. The minimum amount for RTGS is ₹2,00,000, with no upper ceiling.

claims.claim: This is a specific annual holiday observed on April 1st for banks to close their financial year accounts.
claims.note: While April 1st is historically associated with bank's closing of accounts, the RBI holiday calendar primarily lists holidays under the Negotiable Instruments Act. It's a practice rather than a universally declared holiday under the NI Act for public transactions.

claims.claim: NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer): The RBI made NEFT available 24x7, 365 days a year, since December 2019. So, you can initiate NEFT transfers even on a bank holiday, and they will be processed.
claims.note: NEFT system is available round the clock throughout the year on all days (24x7x365 basis) since December 16, 2019.

claims.claim: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) and UPI (Unified Payments Interface) are particularly useful for instant transfers even on holidays.
claims.note: IMPS offers an instant, 24x7, interbank electronic fund transfer service. UPI payments are also available 24x7.

article_title: Planning Your Finances Around Upcoming Bank Holidays
